sources.name: Sukuma Speech Corpus (read speech)
sources.description: Read-speech ASR corpus with per-utterance speaker metadata (gender, age group, region, district, recording environment, estimated SNR). Largest Sukuma speech corpus found.
sources.citation: joseph-telemala, Sukuma Speech Corpus, Hugging Face, 2026.
sources.notes: Last updated 2026-09-07. The card does not say where the prompt sentences come from; check before republishing transcripts. Audio size is not listed on the card; expect several GB.

sources.name: Sukuma Voices (ACL release)
sources.description: Transcribed Bible readings released with the LoResLM 2026 paper. Includes two synthetic (TTS) test sets for speech-quality evaluation. The paper's ASR baseline is reported on this release.
sources.citation: Mgonzo, M., Oketch, K., Etori, N. A., Mang'eni, W., Nyaki, E. F., & Mollel, M. S. (2026). Learning from Scarcity: Building and Benchmarking Speech Technology for Sukuma. LoResLM 2026, pp. 288-296. https://aclanthology.org/2026.loreslm-1.25/
sources.notes: Transcripts are inside the audio parquet files, so text needs --audio. The Hugging Face card says Apache-2.0; the project's GitHub repo uses CC BY 4.0. Baseline: Whisper Large v3 fine-tune, 25.19% final WER (sartify/sukuma-voices README).

sources.name: Sukuma Voices (full release)
sources.description: Larger Sukuma Voices release of Bible narrative readings, single train split.
sources.citation: Sartify Company Limited, Sukuma Voices, 2025. https://github.com/sartify/sukuma-voices
sources.notes: About 8 GB of WAV-in-parquet. Stats are from the GitHub README; the Hugging Face viewer shows ~7.99k rows, so counts may differ by release.

sources.name: AfriSpeech africa-corpus: Sukuma Bible text
sources.description: Verse-keyed text of three Sukuma Bible translations harvested from YouVersion: Sukuma New Testament 2000 (id 1512, SNT00), Bibilia Ilagano Lya Kale 2015 (id 1517, SUKBI15) and Ilagano Ipya Lya (id 2684, SUK60). Main text corpus for this project.
sources.citation: AfriSpeech, africa-corpus-builder and the AfriSpeech/africa-corpus dataset.
sources.notes: The builder's own license table marks all three Sukuma versions as NOT public domain, so its default public-domain mode returns no Sukuma text. Use for local research only; never commit this text. Sentence count is from the builder README. scripts/download_afrispeech_text.py turns these files into data/sukuma_sentences.csv.

sources.name: FineWeb-2 (suk_Latn)
sources.description: Common Crawl web text identified as Sukuma by language ID.
sources.citation: Penedo, G. et al. FineWeb2: One Pipeline to Scale Them All. Hugging Face, 2024.
sources.notes: Small and unverified: language-ID filtered web text often mixes in Swahili or other languages. Audit before training. Also subject to Common Crawl terms of use.

sources.name: FinePDFs (suk_Latn)
sources.description: Text extracted from PDFs on the web, identified as Sukuma by language ID.
sources.notes: Largest open Sukuma text source found besides the Bible. Same caveat as FineWeb-2: audit language ID quality and check for Bible duplicates.

sources.name: GlotCC-V1 (suk-Latn)
sources.description: Cleaned Common Crawl text for minority languages, Sukuma subset.
sources.citation: Kargaran, A. H. et al. GlotCC: An Open Broad-Coverage CommonCrawl Corpus and Pipeline for Minority Languages. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks.
sources.notes: CC0 covers the packaging; underlying pages remain under Common Crawl terms. If the text column is not named 'content', fetch_data.py falls back to 'text'.

sources.name: DCAD-2000 (suk_Latn)
sources.description: Re-cleaned FineWeb-2 Sukuma text, split into kept and removed documents by anomaly detection.
sources.citation: DCAD-2000: A Multilingual Dataset across 2000+ Languages with Data Cleaning as Anomaly Detection. NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks.
sources.notes: Derived from FineWeb-2, so it mostly overlaps fineweb2-suk. Useful as a second opinion on which documents are clean.

sources.name: PanLex expressions (suk)
sources.description: Sukuma expressions and their meanings from the PanLex 2024-03-01 database dump.
sources.citation: Kamholz, D., Pool, J., & Colowick, S. (2014). PanLex: Building a Resource for Panlingual Lexical Translation. LREC 2014.
sources.notes: CC0, so it can be committed to data/open once fetched and reviewed.

sources.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Sukuma, with Swahili and English)
sources.description: Full UDHR text in Sukuma (translation credited to UNDP Tanzania by OHCHR), plus the Swahili and English versions for article-level parallel use.
sources.citation: United Nations, Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Sukuma translation, UNDP Tanzania). Text via the Unicode UDHR project as packaged in NLTK data (udhr2).
sources.notes: Committed under data/open/udhr/. Only general-domain, non-religious Sukuma text found.

sources.name: ASJP wordlist: Sukuma
sources.description: Basic-vocabulary wordlist (up to 40 concepts) for Sukuma from the Automated Similarity Judgment Program.
sources.citation: Wichmann, S., Holman, E. W., & Brown, C. H. (eds.). The ASJP Database. Lexibank CLDF edition (lexibank/asjp).
sources.notes: Committed under data/open/lexicon/. Forms are in ASJPcode, a simplified phonetic ASCII alphabet, not standard Sukuma spelling.

sources.name: Grollemund et al. Bantu wordlists: Sukuma and Ntuzu
sources.description: 100-concept basic-vocabulary wordlists for two Sukuma varieties (Sukuma, Ntuzu) with cognate-set IDs, from the Bantu phylogeny study.
sources.citation: Grollemund, R., Branford, S., Bostoen, K., Meade, A., Venditti, C., & Pagel, M. (2015). Bantu expansion shows that habitat alters the route and pace of human dispersals. PNAS 112(43).
sources.notes: Committed under data/open/lexicon/. NonCommercial license: fine for this academic project, but anyone reusing it commercially must drop this file.

sources.name: Grambank: Sukuma grammatical features
sources.description: Coded values for Grambank's 195 grammatical features for Sukuma (0 = absent, 1 = present, ? = unknown, plus multi-value features).
sources.citation: Skirgård, H. et al. (2023). Grambank reveals the importance of genealogical constraints on linguistic diversity and highlights the impact of language loss. Science Advances 9(16).

sources.name: WALS: Sukuma features
sources.description: World Atlas of Language Structures feature values for Sukuma (WALS code skm).
sources.citation: Dryer, M. S. & Haspelmath, M. (eds.) (2013). The World Atlas of Language Structures Online. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7385533
sources.notes: Committed under data/open/typology/. WALS cites Batibo (1985) for Sukuma.

sources.name: PHOIBLE: Sukuma phoneme inventory
sources.description: Phoneme inventory for Sukuma (PHOIBLE inventory 1568): vowels with length, prenasalized and breathy consonants, and tones.
sources.citation: Moran, S. & McCloy, D. (eds.) (2019). PHOIBLE 2.0. Jena: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History. https://phoible.org/
sources.notes: Committed under data/open/phonology/. Useful for the normalizer and diacritic restorer: shows which vowel-length and tone contrasts the writing system has to carry.

sources.name: Global Recordings Network: Kisukuma
sources.description: Evangelistic audio recordings and scripts in Kisukuma.
sources.citation: Global Recordings Network, Kisukuma language page.
sources.notes: Not downloaded automatically. Untranscribed, so mainly useful as extra listening or test material with permission.
